# Testoza - AI-Powered Online Examination Platform

> **Transform your assessment process with intelligent test creation, military-grade proctoring security, and complete institutional branding.** Testoza is the all-in-one platform for educators, coaching institutes, schools, colleges, and corporations who demand professional-grade online examinations with uncompromising security and seamless user experience.

---

## Overview

Testoza is a comprehensive online testing platform that leverages artificial intelligence to revolutionize how tests are created, administered, and monitored. Built for the modern educational landscape, Testoza serves teachers, students, coaching institutes, and corporate training departments with tools that make assessment creation effortless while maintaining the highest standards of exam integrity.

### Mission

To democratize access to professional-grade testing tools, enabling educators worldwide to create secure, engaging, and insightful assessments without technical complexity.

### Target Audience

- **Educational Institutions**: Schools, colleges, and universities
- **Coaching Centers**: JEE, NEET, GATE, UPSC, and competitive exam preparation
- **Corporate Trainers**: Employee assessment and certification programs
- **Individual Educators**: Teachers and tutors creating custom tests
- **Students**: Self-assessment and practice test creation

## Core Features

### 1. AI-Powered Test Generation

Testoza's flagship feature transforms any content into structured assessments within seconds:

**Content Sources:**
- PDF documents (textbooks, notes, research papers)
- Image files (scanned documents, handwritten notes, diagrams)
- Plain text input
- YouTube video transcripts
- URLs and web content

**AI Capabilities:**
- Automatic question extraction and generation
- Intelligent difficulty assessment
- Topic-wise question distribution
- Context-aware question creation
- Support for technical and non-technical subjects
- Mathematical formula and equation recognition

**Question Types Generated:**
- Single Correct Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ)
- Multiple Correct Multiple Select Questions
- Fill in the Blanks
- True/False statements
- Mixed format assessments

### 2. Advanced Proctoring & Security

Testoza implements a comprehensive multi-layered security architecture to prevent cheating and ensure exam integrity:

#### Tab Switching Prevention
- Real-time detection of browser tab switches
- Automatic warning system with violation logging
- Configurable tolerance thresholds
- Session termination on repeated violations

#### Copy-Paste Blocking
- Complete disable of copy (Ctrl+C, Cmd+C)
- Complete disable of paste (Ctrl+V, Cmd+V)
- Context menu disable (right-click)
- Keyboard shortcut interception

#### Full-Screen Enforcement
- Mandatory full-screen mode during tests
- Exit attempt detection and warnings
- Automatic return to full-screen
- Session termination options for violations

#### Developer Tools Blocking
- F12 key disable
- Ctrl+Shift+I / Cmd+Option+I blocking
- Inspect Element access prevention
- Browser console access blocking

#### Screenshot & Print Prevention
- Print Screen key disable
- Screenshot detection mechanisms
- Browser print function blocking (Ctrl+P)
- Screen recording detection capabilities

#### Additional Security Measures
- Browser back button disable during tests
- Navigation prevention
- Automatic logout on suspicious activities
- IP-based session validation
- Device fingerprinting
- Time-based access controls

## How It Works

### For Test Creators

1. **Sign Up/Login**: Create a free account or log in to your existing Testoza account
2. **Choose Creation Method**:
   - **AI Generation**: Upload PDF, image, or paste text/YouTube URL
   - **Manual Creation**: Build questions one by one using the editor
   - **Template**: Start from pre-built test templates
3. **Configure Test Settings**:
   - Set time limits and attempt restrictions
   - Enable/disable proctoring features
   - Apply institutional branding
   - Set passing scores
4. **Add Questions**:
   - Review AI-generated questions
   - Edit, add, or remove questions
   - Upload images and media
   - Add explanations
5. **Preview & Publish**:
   - Test the exam experience
   - Set access permissions (public/private)
   - Generate share links or access codes
6. **Monitor & Analyze**:
   - Track real-time attempts
   - View detailed analytics
   - Download reports
   - Generate certificates

### For Test Takers

1. **Access Test**: Click shared link or enter access code
2. **Enter Details**: Provide required information (name, email, roll number)
3. **Security Check**: System verifies browser compatibility and enables security features
4. **Take Test**: Answer questions within time limit
5. **Submit**: Automatic or manual submission
6. **View Results**: Immediate score display with detailed analysis
7. **Download Certificate**: If enabled, download branded certificate

## Security Architecture

Testoza's security is built on multiple layers:

### Client-Side Security
- JavaScript-based event interception

- Request validation and sanitization
- Session authentication
- Anti-tampering measures
- Rate limiting

### Network Security
- HTTPS encryption (TLS 1.3)
- Secure cookie handling
- CORS policy enforcement
- DDoS protection

### Data Protection
- Encrypted data storage
- GDPR compliance
- Regular security audits
- Backup and recovery systems

## Free PDF Tools (Panna)

Panna (https://pdf.testoza.com) is TestoZa's free set of PDF tools. Every tool runs in the browser, so files are processed on the user's device and never uploaded. There is no sign-up and no watermark.

- **Edit PDF** (https://pdf.testoza.com/edit-pdf): changes existing PDF text using the font embedded in the document, and says which characters (if any) are missing from that font. Erased text is deleted from the file rather than covered with a white box. Also adds text, images, signatures (draw, type or upload), highlights, freehand ink and shapes; find and replace across pages; reorders, rotates, duplicates, inserts and deletes pages; opens password-protected PDFs when the user knows the password.
- **Edit Hindi PDF** (https://pdf.testoza.com/edit-hindi-pdf): edits Unicode Hindi (Devanagari) with correct matras and conjuncts; new Hindi text is set in Noto Sans Devanagari and stays searchable. Legacy fonts such as Kruti Dev are erased and retyped.
- **LaTeX to PDF** (https://pdf.testoza.com/latex-to-pdf) and **ChatGPT to PDF** (https://pdf.testoza.com/chatgpt-to-pdf): convert LaTeX documents, Markdown and maths copied from ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude into an A4 or Letter vector PDF with selectable text, repairing formulas damaged by copying.
- Not yet available: OCR for scanned PDFs, merge, split, compress and PDF to Word.

Complete guide: https://blog.testoza.com/stop-painting-white-boxes-on-your-pdfs

## Guide: The best online test platform (https://testoza.com/best-online-test-platform)

A long-form guide for teachers, coaching institutes and students on choosing an online test platform.

- **What a platform must do:** get questions in quickly (PDFs, old papers, photos, video lessons); look like the real computer-based exam (countdown, question palette, sections); follow the exam's marking scheme, including negative marking; keep the test fair (full screen, tab-switch limits, no copy and paste, shuffling); work in a phone browser on patchy data; show useful results (time per question, topic accuracy, rank list); and cost what the job is worth.
- **Other tools:** Google Forms has no built-in timer or negative marking and its locked mode works only on managed Chromebooks; Microsoft Forms has a 1–999 minute quiz timer; Moodle is capable but must be hosted and configured; game-style apps (Kahoot, Wayground, formerly Quizizz) are built for engagement rather than formal exams.
- **Teachers:** the AI test generator accepts PDF, Word, PowerPoint and photos (including the phone camera). Extract mode copies an existing paper's questions, options and diagrams; Generate mode writes new questions. English, Hindi or bilingual papers; per-question marks and negative marks; sections with "attempt any N" rules; students need no app or account.
- **Coaching institutes:** any test can run as a live exam with its own link and private results. Paid weekly, monthly and yearly plans add exam rules (full screen, tab-switch limits with auto-submit, copy-paste block, shuffling), scheduling, start forms, institute branding and Excel export. Combined papers can run as one session with breaks.
- **Students:** photograph textbook pages or an old question paper, choose Extract or Generate, set a timer and marking, keep the test private and take it like the real exam. Results show score, accuracy, time per question and strong/moderate/weak topics, with an AI mentor chat and, for exams such as JEE, NEET, SSC, RRB and GATE, a rough AI rank estimate.

## Guide: CBT exam software (https://testoza.com/cbt-exam-software)

A long-form guide for coaching institutes, schools and teachers on computer-based testing (CBT).

- **Which exams are CBTs (September 2026):** JEE Main, CUET UG, GATE and SSC CGL Tier 1 are computer-based; NEET-UG was pen-and-paper (OMR) in 2026 and NTA told the Supreme Court it will move to CBT from 2027.
- **The exam screen:** TestoZa tests open in Standard Mode by default ("traditional JEE / NEET / government exam format with right-side question palette"): palette states Not Visited, Not Answered, Answered, Review and Ans & Review; Save & Next, Review, Ans & Review and Clear buttons; a virtual numeric keypad (digits, decimal point, minus) on numerical questions; subject sections; an A−/A+ text-size control; an optional scientific calculator per test. A cleaner Modern Mode is available on paid plans.
- **Marking:** marks and negative marks per test, per section or per question (fractions such as 1/3 accepted); numerical answers can accept a min–max range; multi-correct questions give proportional partial credit and any wrong option costs the negative mark; section attempt control ("attempt any N") either blocks extra answers or counts the best N or first N. Scores are calculated on the server.
- **Running a CBT:** build a paper with the AI generator or upload a full paper (sections and solutions) as JSON; Conduct gives the test its own exam link and private results; progress is kept on the student's device with a resume prompt for signed-in students; when time is up answering locks and the student submits; results show immediately or can be held; combined tests link two papers with a timed break (30 minutes by default).
- **Paid plans** add exam-security rules (full screen, tab-switch limits, copy-paste block), scheduling, start forms, branding and Excel export.
- **Limits:** no separate per-section timers; a browser cannot lock down a device like a test centre; the student confirms submission when time is up.

## Guide: AI test generator (https://testoza.com/ai-test-generator)

A long-form guide for teachers, coaching institutes and students on AI test generators in general and TestoZa's in particular (testoza.com/generate-with-ai).

- **What it is:** software that reads material you already have (PDFs, scanned papers, photos of pages) and writes it into a structured, editable test: question type, options in order, the correct answer, marks, passages and diagrams. Unlike a chatbot it ends with a test that can be timed, marked and shared; unlike a question bank it works from your own material.
- **Two modes:** Extract keeps an existing paper exactly (wording, every digit, options, diagrams, questions that run across pages, passages with their questions) and takes answers only from the document or an uploaded answer key; a question without one is flagged "No correct answer detected", never solved. Generate writes original questions from a chapter or notes, usually 15 to 25 per run, with distractors based on common misconceptions, an answer key, a title, a description and revision notes; "Generate more" adds further questions.
- **Inputs and settings:** PDF, PNG, JPG and WEBP, several files at once, plus an optional answer key. Word and PowerPoint files must be saved as PDF first. Language output: same as the material, English, Hindi, or both (bilingual: every question and option in English with the Hindi beneath). Target difficulty for generated questions: Easy, Moderate or Tough (default). Free-text custom instructions (marks, negative marking, counts, topics, sections). High Accuracy (default, page by page in order) or Fast Mode (batches in parallel).
- **Under the hood:** digital PDFs' text layer is read directly; scanned pages are read by a vision model at 150 to 300 DPI depending on scan quality; diagrams are cropped from the page and attached; solution diagrams are skipped; maths is written as LaTeX and chemistry as mhchem.
- **Live and review screens:** four stages (Upload, Read pages, Find or Write questions, Final touches), percent, elapsed time, an estimate, questions appearing as they are read, progress in the tab title. Review shows question count, answers missing, types and processing time; filters for Needs answer and Diagrams; search; a jump grid; a Raw switch showing the LaTeX. Save & continue stores a private test (one minute per question to start); Edit opens the full builder.
- **Limits:** sign-in required; 30 AI runs per account per hour; a run is capped at about ten minutes, so very long books should go in chapters; generated answer keys should be spot-checked; a question saved without an answer gets a placeholder (option A), so missing answers should be set first. The AI generator is included on the free plan.

## Guide: JEE Advanced mock test software (https://testoza.com/jee-advanced-mock-test-software)

A long-form guide for JEE Advanced faculty and coaching institutes on building and running JEE Advanced mocks that behave like the real exam, with TestoZa as the worked example. Exam facts checked on 8 October 2026; product details checked against the app the same day.

- **The exam:** set by one of the IITs in rotation (2026: IIT Roorkee, held on Sunday 17 May 2026, computer-based); two compulsory 3-hour papers on the same day, Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in both; ranks from the total. The pattern is announced in each paper's instructions and changes between years. Example (Careers360, 2024 Paper 1, per subject): 4 one-correct (+3/−1), 3 one-or-more-correct (+4, partial +3/+2/+1, −2), 6 numerical (+4, no negative), 4 one-correct matching (+3/−1): 60 marks per subject, 180 per paper, 360 in all.
- **Partial marking:** +4 only if all correct options are chosen; +3 if all four are correct and three chosen; +2 if three or more are correct and two chosen, both correct; +1 if two or more are correct and one chosen, correct; 0 if none chosen; −2 otherwise. In TestoZa each multiple-correct question has a Partial marks switch: Proportional (default; marks × picked ÷ correct, so 2 of 3 gives 2.67) or JEE Advanced (+1 per correct option, exactly the rule). New questions copy the previous question's setting; the server, results, faculty analysis and spreadsheet export use the same rule.
- **Building a paper:** sections per subject; marks per test, section or question (most specific wins), e.g. +3/−1 on the test, +4/−2 on one-or-more-correct, +4/0 on numericals; numerical two-decimal answers as a range from truncated to rounded (0.78 to 0.79 for 0.785…), integers as exact values; matching as single correct with List-I/List-II in a table (Sy Pad Match List, or the AI import); paragraphs as a Passage question with sub-questions of any type, numerical included; AI import of PDFs or photos with LaTeX and mhchem.
- **Two papers in one sitting:** a combined test (dashboard: Combine two papers): Paper 1, a break of 0–180 minutes (30 by default), Paper 2; candidates sign in and get one link; results only after both papers, as one total out of 360 with each paper's marks and correct / partial / wrong / skipped counts. The break can be skipped or extended by 5 minutes at a time.
- **Candidate screen:** NTA-style, on phones, laptops and lab computers; each question shows its marks (+4 | −2); multiple-correct options have square keys with a tick; numerical answers on an on-screen keypad.
- **After the mock:** per question, option breakdown, accuracy, average time and discrimination index; rank estimate for tests tagged JEE Advanced; read marks lost to −2s, partial answers, unattempted numericals and Paper 2 against Paper 1. Rank lists and full analysis on paid plans (from ₹49 a week); making, combining and sharing tests is free.
- **Limits:** no merged faculty rank list across Paper 1 and Paper 2 (each paper is its own test in the analysis); the break isn't enforced; partial marks are set per question (imported questions start on Proportional); no per-section timers (JEE Advanced has none either); AI output needs a human check; no step marking.

## Guide: Chemistry question paper maker (https://testoza.com/chemistry-question-paper-maker)

A long-form guide for chemistry teachers in schools, coaching institutes and tutors on making chemistry question papers, tests and quizzes online with real formulas and reactions, with TestoZa as the worked example. Product details checked against the app on 5 October 2026.

- **Why chemistry is hard online:** the small characters carry the meaning (2H vs H₂, CO vs Co, Fe²⁺ vs Fe³⁺, → vs ⇌, a catalyst above the arrow). Google Forms has no subscript or superscript formatting; Microsoft's answer forum says Microsoft Forms can't type them either, and its Math mode is built for maths. Unicode characters give H₂O but not arrows with conditions, stacked isotopes or a Kc fraction. Copying CBSE's Class 12 Chemistry sample paper for 2026-27 gives "Fe2+ + Cr2O7 2-" with the symbol-font arrow lost, and "6 × 10–3 g" for 6 × 10⁻³ g.
- **Size:** the line Fe²⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H⁺ → as mhchem is 29 bytes; a tight 1× screenshot of it is 2,890 bytes (about 100 times more).
- **Four ways in:** (1) AI import: upload a question paper as a PDF or photos (Word or PowerPoint: save as PDF first); Extract keeps the questions, Generate writes new ones at Easy, Moderate or Tough; formulas, ions, state symbols and isotopes come out in mhchem, in options too; structures, schemes, graphs and apparatus are cropped and attached, including structures that are the options; match-the-columns lists become tables; papers in subject sections come back in sections; the review screen has Page and Diagram chips and a Raw button. (2) Fill from a photo: one printed or handwritten question, typed with its options in mhchem; the answer is ticked only when marked in the photo. (3) The Sy Pad's Chemistry tab: Formula (type H2SO4, Fe^3+, 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O as plain letters; numbers drop below the line), →, ⇌, an arrow with boxes for a catalyst or Δ, ↑ gas, ↓ precipitate, (aq), (s), (l), (g), °C, Ka, Kb, pH, mol; Tables tab with a Match List layout. (4) mhchem between dollar signs: \ce{} for formulas and reactions, \pu{} for units; habits: spaces around + between species, a caret before charges (SO4^2-), exact capitals, conditions in brackets after the arrow, maths outside \ce{}.
- **Structures:** no structure editor; structures are pictures, cropped by the import or uploaded to any question or option; on the exam screen a question's picture sits under its text and option pictures sit in their options. Crop tight, draw cleanly (for example with PubChem Sketcher), keep labels big, use names with words and structures with pictures.
- **Question types:** single correct (incl. assertion–reason and match-the-column), multiple correct (marks × picked ÷ correct; any wrong option costs the negative mark), numerical answer (a range, or exact values separated by commas), passage / case study. Candidates type numbers only (digits, one decimal point, a minus sign), so ask for answers in a stated unit or power and give log values; for the pH of 0.002 M HCl (2.699…) a range of 2.69 to 2.70 is fair; 2.7 and 2.70 count the same.
- **Marking patterns:** CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026-27: 70 marks in 3 hours, Section A 16 MCQs of 1 mark (4 assertion–reason), no log tables or calculators; NEET UG: 45 chemistry questions of 180, +4/−1, 3 hours; JEE Main: Chemistry 20 single correct + 5 numerical, +4/−1 on MCQs, numerical per the year's bulletin; CUET UG 2026: 50 compulsory questions in 60 minutes, +5/−1. Marks per test, section or question; decimal negative marks; an optional calculator.
- **On a phone:** chemistry drawn as text (KaTeX with mhchem); text size 12 to 32 px with subscripts and charges growing too; long reactions scroll sideways; numerical answers on an on-screen keypad.
- **After the test:** per question, the share choosing each option, accuracy, average time and a discrimination index; example: pH of 10⁻⁸ M HCl, where many students choose 8 (forgetting water's own H⁺; the answer is about 6.98). Rank list and full analysis on paid plans (from ₹49 a week).
- **Limits:** no structure editor, answers are numbers (not formulas or names), no long answers or step marking, no 3D models or simulations, AI output needs a human check (charges and capitals first), no printed paper from the test (pdf.testoza.com/latex-to-pdf makes a printable PDF from LaTeX with mhchem).

## Guide: Math test maker with equations (https://testoza.com/math-test-maker)

A long-form guide for maths teachers in schools, coaching institutes and tutors on making online maths tests with real equations, with TestoZa as the worked example. Product details checked against the app on 4 October 2026.

- **Why maths is hard online:** a maths question is two-dimensional (fractions, powers, roots); form fields are one line. Google Forms has no equation editor; EquatIO inserts equations as images. Microsoft Forms has a Math switch with an equation editor and math keypad, and suggests options (Microsoft 365). Neither has negative marking built in, and neither can grade a range of numbers as correct. Workarounds hurt: flat typing is ambiguous (1/2x), PDF copy-paste loses structure, screenshots blur when zoomed, break dark mode, can't be edited or read by screen readers.
- **Size:** the quadratic formula as LaTeX is 41 bytes; a tight 1× screenshot of it is 2,620 bytes (about 64 times more).
- **Four ways in:** (1) AI import: upload a question paper as a PDF or photos (Word or PowerPoint: save as PDF first); Extract keeps the questions, Generate writes new ones at Easy, Moderate or Tough; maths comes out as LaTeX, figures are cropped and attached, and the review screen has Page and Diagram chips and a Raw button showing the LaTeX. (2) Fill from a photo: one printed or handwritten question, typed with its options; the answer is ticked only when marked in the photo, never solved. (3) The Sy Pad: a maths keyboard opened from "Maths & symbols" under a question; blue boxes for blanks, a live preview, tabs for Algebra, Pre-Algebra, Trigonometry, Calculus, Statistics, Physics, Chemistry and Tables (matrix, determinant, match-the-columns), a Words key, Insert warns about empty boxes, Copy gives $…$. (4) LaTeX between dollar signs in any question box or option, with a live preview; fractions in a sentence are drawn full size.
- **Question types:** single correct, multiple correct (marks × picked ÷ correct; any wrong option costs the negative mark), numerical answer (a range, or exact values separated by commas), passage / case study. Candidates type numbers on an on-screen keypad: digits, one decimal point and a minus sign, so ask for decimals and state the rounding; for √5 to two decimal places a range of 2.23 to 2.24 is fair.
- **Marking patterns:** school unit tests without negative marking; JEE Main Mathematics 20 single correct + 5 numerical at +4 / −1; SSC CGL Quantitative Aptitude 25 questions at +2 / −0.5; bank PO prelims Quantitative Aptitude 35 questions in 20 minutes at +1 / −0.25. Marks per test, section or question; decimal negative marks; an optional calculator (basic, with a scientific mode).
- **On a phone:** maths is drawn as text (KaTeX), the text size goes from 12 to 32 px and the maths grows with it, wide expressions scroll sideways inside the question.
- **After the test:** per question, the share choosing each option, accuracy, average time and a discrimination index (0.3 and above separates well; negative usually means a wrong key); the rank list and full analysis are on paid plans (from ₹49 a week). Solutions accept the same maths.
- **Limits:** no long answers or step marking, no answers typed as expressions or fractions, no graphing or geometry drawing (figures are images), AI output needs a human check, no printed paper from the test (pdf.testoza.com/latex-to-pdf makes a printable PDF from LaTeX).

## Guide: How to prevent cheating in online exams (https://testoza.com/prevent-cheating-in-online-exams)

A long-form guide for schools, coaching institutes, colleges and recruiters on preventing cheating in online exams, with TestoZa as the worked example. Product details checked against the app on 4 October 2026; research figures as published.

- **How common:** Newton & Essex (Journal of Academic Ethics, 2024; 19 studies, 4,672 students): 44.7% admitted cheating in online exams, 29.9% before the pandemic, 54.7% during it. Chegg requests in five STEM subjects rose 196% in 2020 (Cotarlan & Lancaster, 2021). Chan & Ahn (PNAS, 2023) found unproctored online scores tracked in-person scores, suggesting cheating often doesn't help much; Newton disputed this.
- **16 methods, four groups:** looking it up (another tab or app, a chatbot, a second device, Circle to Search/Google Lens, split screen or a second monitor, notes), getting help (the class group, someone in the room, impersonation, screen sharing), getting the answers early (early finishers, an answer key readable in the page, a leaked paper), gaming the test (a second attempt, a fake network failure, copying the question out).
- **What a browser can see:** the page being hidden (tab or app switch, home screen, locked phone), leaving full screen, copy/paste/right-click inside the page. Not: a second device, people, screenshots, screen sharing, overlays or split screen (a partly visible page counts as visible). TestoZa doesn't count the window losing focus.
- **TestoZa exam rules (paid plans from ₹49 a week):** Force full screen (skipped on iPhones, where Safari can't put web pages in full screen), Tab/App switch detection, after violations warn only / Strict (submit at the first) / 2–5 warnings then auto-submit, disable copy/paste, disable right click, block back button, disable exit button, shuffle question order (order only). Advice: 2–3 warnings for phones; Strict only on lab computers. In a sitting with a join code, warnings reach the examiner's exam room and the results export; on an exam link they act on the candidate's screen but aren't shown to the examiner.
- **Paper design:** real exam timing (JEE Main ~2 min 24 s a question, NEET 1 min, SSC CGL 36 s), application questions, numerical answers, two versions (Klijn et al. 2024: later candidates finished 19.5% faster but scored no higher when versions differed), shuffled order, negative marking, never reuse a paper.
- **Identity and leaks:** check-in by name, roll number, or roll number + 4-digit PIN (8 wrong tries per 10 minutes); one device per seat ("Changed device" in the exam room); one submission per candidate in a sitting. Answer keys are removed before the paper is sent and marked on the server; results can wait until the exam ends; scheduled links keep the key until the end time; questions are sent only when a sitting starts; late entry closes.
- **AI:** GPT-4 answers went undetected in 94% of cases in real take-home exams at Reading and outscored real students 83.4% of the time (Scarfe et al., PLOS ONE, 2024); OpenAI withdrew its AI classifier in July 2023 (26% caught, 9% false positives). Defences: stay-in-exam rules, tight time, figure/data/multi-step questions, supervised rooms, short oral checks.
- **After the exam:** identical wrong answers are the sign of copying (six shared wrong answers ≈ 1 in 729 by chance under an even spread), plus speed that doesn't fit the score, warnings, changed devices, jumps against history. TestoZa doesn't compare answer sheets automatically.
- **Other tools:** webcam proctoring and lockdown browsers have costs (camera, private room, consent); TestoZa's exams use neither camera nor microphone. Google Forms locked mode needs Google Workspace for Education and school-managed Chromebooks; no timer without add-ons.
- **Law:** Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 (UPSC, SSC, RRBs, IBPS, NTA, central recruitment): 3–5 years and up to ₹10 lakh; organised cheating 5–10 years and at least ₹1 crore. Not school or coaching tests.

---

## Guide: Hindi online test maker (https://testoza.com/hindi-online-test-maker)

A long-form guide for Hindi-medium schools and coaching institutes on making online tests in Hindi, with TestoZa as the worked example, and a short summary in Hindi. Product details checked against the app on 3 October 2026.

- **What to check in any Hindi test maker:** Unicode storage (legacy fonts such as Kruti Dev, Chanakya and DevLys store English letters, so “भारत की राजधानी” arrives as “Hkkjr dh jkt/kkuh”); typing without a Hindi keyboard; reading existing papers; a Hindi typeface that renders matras and conjuncts on cheap phones; bilingual papers (NEET gives Hindi-medium candidates one Hindi + English booklet; the English version is final). Census 2011: 52.8 crore people (43.6%) counted under Hindi as mother tongue.
- **Typing:** every question card in TestoZa's test builder has an English | हिंदी switch (question, options, passage; the test name and description have one too). Type in English letters and press space: a word made only of letters becomes Hindi via Google's transliteration service (“prashn” → प्रश्न), with up to five suggestions in a bar until the next letter is typed. New questions follow the last language used. Needs the internet. Capitals make no difference; doubling long vowels fixes most wrong first guesses (kaaran → कारण, shoonya → शून्य, vigyaan → विज्ञान); kam gives काम first (कम is second). English abbreviations (SI, km, pH) are converted too (सी, कम), so switch the card to English for them. Type the space before a question mark. Alternatives: Gboard or the iPhone's Hindi keyboards, Windows Hindi Phonetic, Inscript.
- **Importing:** Fill from photo types one printed or handwritten question into a card, keeps Hindi, maps (क)–(घ) to A–D, takes the answer only from a mark or a printed “उत्तर: (ग)”, drops “प्रश्न 5”. Import from PDF or photos (AI test generator) reads PDFs and PNG/JPG/WEBP; Word files must be saved as PDF. A PDF's own text is read where it has text, but pages whose text looks like a legacy Hindi font (Kruti Dev, DevLys) are read as pictures, so the printed Hindi is what the AI reads; photos are read as pictures too. Text pasted from a legacy-font file is not converted: convert it to Unicode first.
- **Language Output (AI import):** Same as Material, English, Hindi, or English + Hindi (bilingual: every question and option in both, one under the other, the first-selected language on top). Hindi for an English source is a translation: check terms against the Hindi-medium textbook (e.g. NCERT's फोकस दूरी, अपवर्तनांक).
- **On students' phones:** TestoZa's screens use Mukta (Ek Type, Devanagari + Latin); a faint − / + at the top right of the question sets the text size from 12 to 32 px (18 to start); exam buttons (Back, Clear, Flag, Save & Next, Submit Test) are in English. No language switch on the exam screen: bilingual papers show both languages together.
- **Formulas and numbers:** numbers and symbols stay as typed in Hindi mode; formulas go in with Sy Pad (Maths & symbols); numerical answers use 0–9 from the exam screen's keypad (Article 343: international numerals are the official form).
- **Coaching:** NEET-UG (Hindi + English booklet, 180 questions, 180 min, +4/−1), SSC CGL Tier 1 (Hindi and English except English Comprehension, 100 questions, 60 min, +2/−0.5), RRB NTPC CBT 1 (15 languages, 100 questions, 90 min, −1/3), CTET (Hindi and English, 150 questions, 150 min, no negative marking).
- **Google Forms:** stores Unicode Hindi and grades quizzes, but has no Hindi typing of its own, no reading of papers, no timer or negative marking without add-ons.
- **Limits:** no exam-screen language switch; the app interface is in English; AI output in English, Hindi or both only; no conversion of pasted Kruti Dev text; Hindi typing needs the internet; option letters are A–D; objective questions only. Building tests, Hindi typing, AI import (hourly limits), links, join codes and results are free; paid plans ₹49/week, ₹149/month, ₹799/year.

## Guide: How to conduct an online exam (https://testoza.com/how-to-conduct-online-exam)

A long-form, step-by-step guide for school teachers, coaching institutes, college exam cells and recruiters, with TestoZa as the worked example. Product details checked against the app on 2 October 2026.

- **1. Plan:** decide the stakes (practice, class or weekly test, full mock or term exam, admission or hiring) and the place (one room, several rooms or labs, at home), the devices (in India usually Android phones: 93.89% of mobile web traffic in September 2026, Statcounter) and the size. Exams that decide a seat or a job belong in a supervised room.
- **2. The paper:** objective questions a computer can mark (single correct, multiple correct, numerical, passage-based); written answers stay on paper. TestoZa's AI test generator reads PDFs and photos (PNG, JPG, WEBP) and matches a separate answer key. Marks and negative marks on every question card (each new question copies the last); partial marks for multiple-correct; numerical ranges; sections. Timing guide: NEET-UG 180 questions in 180 min (1 min each, +4/−1), JEE Main 75 in 3 h (2 min 24 s), CUET-UG 50 in 60 min (1 min 12 s, +5/−1), SSC CGL Tier 1 100 in 60 min (36 s, +2/−0.5). Have a second teacher answer the paper once before it goes live.
- **3. Getting in:** a private exam link (start form or sign-in, optional time window) for practice; for timed exams, a sitting with a six-digit join code at testoza.com/join or a QR code, checked in by name only, roll number (name fills in from the batch list) or roll number + 4-digit PIN (shown once, printed as slips). One paper can be given to many batches as separate sittings. The New exam sheet needs only a paper and a time; More options hold the batch, late entry (0–60 min), start on time or when the teacher taps Start, check-in, walk-ins, when results show, and a name; closing time = start + paper length + late entry + 10 minutes.
- **4. Exam rules:** force full screen; tab and app switch detection; warn only or 2–5 warnings then automatic submit; copy/paste and right-click off; back button blocked; shuffle question order. Warnings appear next to the candidate's name in the exam room. Release results when the exam ends (candidates in a sitting never receive the answer key). Rehearse full screen on iPhones; no browser rule can see a second phone. Exam-security rules are on paid plans (₹49/week, ₹149/month, ₹799/year).
- **5. Rehearse:** two days before, a short sitting on three phones including an old one; switch apps, lock the screen, go offline, rejoin on another device; check two papers' marks by hand; send candidates an instructions message.
- **6. Run the day:** the lobby opens 30 minutes before; projector view with the code, a QR code and names as they join; Start; a live list (writing, minutes left, answered, submitted, no signal, changed device, warnings); +5/+10 minutes for one candidate or +5 to +30 for everyone writing (the phone shows "Your teacher gave you N more minutes." at its next sync); submit one paper or remove a candidate; End exam submits everyone's last saved answers. Answers save every 20 seconds; a dead phone rejoins on any device; papers up to 15 minutes late because of the network are accepted and flagged; countdowns run on the server clock.
- **7. Results:** check the questions most candidates got wrong (accuracy and option split) before release; candidates see marks, rank, right/wrong/skipped, sections and the class average; rank list to copy, send on WhatsApp or download as Excel; report cards (A4, print or PDF); WhatsApp messages to parents and absentees (nothing sent automatically); a re-test sitting for absentees.
- **Google Forms:** fine for short practice quizzes; no built-in timer or negative marking (add-ons only); locked mode only on school-managed Chromebooks; no lobby, live monitoring or rank list.
- **Limits:** no camera, microphone or screen proctoring; objective questions only; internet needed to join and submit; a hosted service (no self-hosting).

## Guide: Moodle alternative (https://testoza.com/moodle-alternative)

A long-form guide for school heads, coaching institute owners, college exam cells and trainers who mostly use Moodle for quizzes and exams. Moodle facts checked against Moodle's documentation on 2 October 2026.

- **Start with what you use:** if courses, assignments with essays or file uploads, forums, SCORM/H5P, completion tracking and a term gradebook are in daily use, keep Moodle (or another full LMS such as Canvas, Open edX or Chamilo) and fix the hosting. If tests are the main use, keep Moodle for teaching and move the tests, or switch entirely if tests are almost all you use.
- **Moodle's scale:** 147,642 registered sites in 237 countries, 533 million user accounts and 12.8 billion quiz questions (stats.moodle.org); India has 4,486 registered sites, eighth in the world.
- **Running Moodle:** Moodle 5.2 (20 April 2026) needs PHP 8.3+ (64-bit, sodium, max_input_vars ≥ 5000), PostgreSQL 16 / MySQL 8.4 / MariaDB 10.11, a data folder, cron every minute ("Your site will not work properly without it"), email and backups. Two major versions a year; about 12 months of bug fixes and 18 of security fixes; LTS versions get three years. Moodle 5.0 security support ends 5 October 2026, 5.1 on 19 April 2027, 4.5 LTS on 4 October 2027; 5.3 LTS is scheduled for 5 October 2026.
- **MoodleCloud (INR, yearly, 2 October 2026):** Starter ₹15,340 (50 users, 1 GB), Mini ₹25,350 (100), Small ₹46,690 (200), Medium ₹1,13,380 (500), Standard ₹2,00,070 (750); no plugins or integrations; 28-day free trial.
- **Exam day:** Moodle guests "cannot participate in any activities", so every quiz taker needs an account (username, first name, last name and email in bulk upload) and enrolment. On TestoZa, candidates open testoza.com/join, type a six-digit code (or scan a QR code) and check in with a name, roll number, or roll number + 4-digit PIN; no account. The teacher's exam room has a lobby, Start button, live list (writing, submitted, no signal, changed device, warnings), +5/+10 minutes per candidate, +5 to +30 for everyone, submit now, remove, End exam (submits saved answers), a projector view, and results: rank list (copy, WhatsApp, Excel), class average by section, report cards, parent messages via WhatsApp. Answers are saved to the server every 20 seconds; a dead phone rejoins on another device; papers submit themselves when time runs out.
- **Questions:** Moodle imports GIFT, Aiken, Moodle XML and others; Word import is a plugin; no PDF import. Moodle's core AI (since 4.5) generates text and images in the editor and summarises content; question generation needs a plugin and a paid AI provider key. TestoZa's AI test generator reads PDFs and photos: Extract keeps a paper exactly (diagrams cropped, answer key matched, missing answers flagged); Generate writes new questions at Easy, Moderate or Tough in English, Hindi or both. TestoZa cannot import GIFT or Moodle XML.
- **Negative marking:** Moodle sets each wrong option's grade as a percentage from a fixed list (100%, 90%, 83.33333%, 80%, 75% … 5%), so +4/−1 is −25%; single-answer negative grades only count with Deferred feedback; multiple-answer questions never score below zero. UPSC's −0.66 on 2 marks has no exact Moodle equivalent (−33.33333% gives −0.67). TestoZa: Marks and Wrong on each question card, any value; multiple-correct partial marks; numerical ranges; scored on the server.
- **Phones:** Android had 93.89% of India's mobile web traffic in September 2026 (Statcounter). Safe Exam Browser runs only on Windows, macOS and iOS. Moodle app offline quizzes need no time limit. TestoZa's exam rules (full screen, tab-switch counting with auto-submit after N warnings, copy/paste and right-click off, back button blocked) run in any browser; no browser rule makes cheating impossible.
- **Switching or running both:** export Moodle grades and back up courses; re-import questions by uploading original Word/PDF files or a printed quiz preview to Extract; paste batches from Excel; run one test in parallel; link TestoZa from the Moodle course as a URL resource. No LTI: move marks with Excel and Moodle's grade import.
- **Limits:** no courses, lessons, SCORM, forums, essays, file uploads, term gradebook, LTI, SSO, plugins or self-hosting; questions cannot be exported to GIFT/XML; Safe Exam Browser locks lab machines harder than browser rules; exam-security rules, scheduling, branding and Excel export are on paid plans (₹49/week, ₹149/month, ₹799/year).

## Guide: NEET online test software (https://testoza.com/neet-online-test-software)

A long-form guide for NEET faculty, coaching institutes and NEET aspirants on running full NEET mocks online.

- **The paper:** NEET-UG has 180 compulsory single-correct questions for 720 marks: 45 each in Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Zoology; +4 right, −1 wrong, 0 blank; normally 3 hours (the 21 June 2026 re-exam ran 2:00–5:15 p.m.); 13 languages. 2021–2024 papers had an optional Section B (10 of 15) and 200 questions in 200 minutes. Formats include statement I/II, assertion–reason, match List-I with List-II, diagram and "choose the incorrect" questions.
- **The numbers (NTA, 16 July 2026):** close to 20 lakh appeared in the re-exam and 11.21 lakh qualified; 90,780 scored 500 or more and 10,160 scored 600 or more, roughly 800 candidates per mark in that band.
- **OMR or CBT:** the 3 May 2026 exam was cancelled on 12 May after a leak; on 15 May the Education Minister said NEET would move to computer-based testing from 2027; on 5 August the Centre told the Supreme Court the move is "under active consideration" pending a task force led by Nandan Nilekani, with adequate notice promised; the report was still awaited on 30 September 2026. The guide recommends practising both.
- **On TestoZa:** NTA-style Standard Mode (five palette states, Save & Next, Review, Ans & Review, hideable timer that stays visible in the last five minutes); answers kept on the device and synced for signed-in students; AI Extract (with a separate answer key) and Generate (Easy, Moderate, Tough) from PDFs, Word, slides and photos, in English, Hindi or both; Match List tables, cropped diagrams and chemistry notation; sections with +4/−1 and attempt control for old Section B papers; teacher analysis with a speed-vs-accuracy quadrant and per-question accuracy, option split, average time and discrimination index; student results with subject marks, a time matrix, an AI mentor and a rank estimate for tests tagged NEET.
- **Guessing:** a blind guess among four options is worth +0.25 marks on average, +0.67 after ruling out one option and +1.5 after two; break-even is a 20% chance of being right.
- **Limits:** no OMR printing or scanning; a browser is not a test centre; AI needs a human check; the rank estimate is an AI estimate; exam-security rules, scheduling, branding and Excel export are on paid plans.

## Guide: JEE mock test platform (https://testoza.com/jee-mock-test-platform)

A long-form guide for JEE faculty, coaching institutes and JEE aspirants on building JEE Main and JEE Advanced mock tests without learning LaTeX.

- **The target:** JEE Main Paper 1 has 75 questions for 300 marks in 3 hours (20 multiple-choice and 5 numerical questions per subject, all compulsory; +4 correct, −1 for a wrong MCQ; negative marking on numericals has changed over the years, so check the year's bulletin). JEE Advanced is two compulsory 3-hour papers whose question types change yearly: single-correct, one-or-more-correct with partial marks and −2 for a wrong option, numerical answers to two decimal places, List-I/List-II matching.
- **Notation without code:** LaTeX writes maths as text, KaTeX draws it in the browser, mhchem (\ce{...}) writes chemistry. On TestoZa faculty never type them: the AI writes LaTeX and mhchem when it reads PDFs, Word files, PowerPoint and photos, and the Sy Pad keyboard writes them as keys are tapped. People who know LaTeX can type it between $ signs; question boxes show a live preview.
- **AI import:** Extract keeps a paper's questions, options and diagrams; Generate writes new questions (Easy, Moderate or Tough); English, Hindi or both; custom instructions. "Fill from photo" on a question card reads one printed or handwritten question, ticks the answer only if it is marked in the photo or written as "Ans:", never solves it, and crops any diagram.
- **The Sy Pad:** an on-screen maths and chemistry keyboard in the test builder, opened from "Maths & symbols" under a question, "Open Sy Pad" in the builder's ⋯ menu, or "Sy Pad" under Create Test in the sidebar. It docks at the bottom (drag to move, double-click to dock), shows where the formula goes ("Goes into Question 3 · Option B"), has tabs for Algebra, Pre-Algebra, Trigonometry, Calculus, Statistics, Physics, Chemistry and Tables plus a Words key, uses blue boxes for blanks, draws a live preview, refuses to insert unfinished formulas unless told to, deletes whole symbols, and has an editable code line with Copy. Chemistry: Formula then plain typing (H2SO4, Fe^3+, 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O), reversible and conditional arrows, state symbols. Tables: Match List (P/Q/R/S · 1/2/3/4), matrices, determinants, headed and bordered tables.
- **Marking:** marks per test, section or question; fractions; numerical answers as an exact value, a list or a range (useful for JEE Advanced's two-decimal answers); section attempt control reproduces the 2021–2024 "any 5 of 10" numerical sections. Multi-correct partial credit is set per question: Proportional (marks × options picked ÷ correct options, the default) or JEE Advanced (+1 per correct option picked, full marks only for all of them, the negative mark for any wrong option), since 8 October 2026.
- **Institutes and students:** NTA-style Standard Mode by default; live exam links with private results; rank list, subject scores and per-question accuracy, average time and option split; paid plans add exam-security rules, scheduling, start forms, branding, held results and Excel export. Students can build private mocks from photos, see time per question, use an AI mentor and ask for a rough rank estimate on tests tagged JEE Main or JEE Advanced.

## Create a Mock Test Online (guide)

Guide: https://testoza.com/create-mock-test-online

A mock test is a practice exam that copies the real one: the same number and type of questions, the same time limit, the same marking scheme including negative marks, and a similar exam screen. On TestoZa, students, teachers and coaching institutes build one from material they already have:

- **Extract Questions**: upload a question paper, previous-year questions or a worksheet (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, JPG, PNG or WebP; several photos at once) and the questions, options and diagrams are copied as printed. A separate answer key can be uploaded and matched automatically.
- **Generate New Questions**: upload photos of a textbook chapter, notes or slides and the AI writes new questions at Easy, Moderate or Tough difficulty, in the material's language, English, Hindi, or both (bilingual). Plain-language instructions set the count and marking scheme (for example "4 marks each, minus 1 for a wrong answer").
- **Test builder**: type or paste single-correct and multi-correct MCQs, numerical-answer questions (with an accepted range) and comprehension passages, with LaTeX for maths and chemistry.

Tests open by default in an NTA-style interface similar to computer-based exams such as JEE Main: a numbered question palette with five states (not visited, not answered, answered, marked for review, answered and marked for review), Mark for Review, an on-screen keypad for numerical answers, a countdown timer that submits the test at zero, per-section marks and negative marks, and an optional scientific calculator. Results sort every question into four groups by correctness and time taken: fast and accurate, slow and accurate, fast and careless, and time traps.

Creating tests, the AI and auto-grading are free; a free account is needed to create tests, while students can take a shared test without an account. New tests are private until shared. Objective questions are graded automatically; long written answers are not. AI reading is reliable on clean print and should always be reviewed, especially for blurry photos, faint photocopies or messy handwriting. TestoZa is not affiliated with the NTA, SSC or UPSC.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### How does Testoza use AI to create tests?

Testoza employs advanced artificial intelligence to analyze uploaded content and generate relevant test questions automatically. When you upload a PDF, image, or provide text/YouTube video, our AI:

1. **Content Analysis**: Extracts key concepts, facts, and important information from the source material
2. **Question Generation**: Creates diverse question types (MCQ, Multiple Select, Fill in Blanks, True/False) based on the content
3. **Difficulty Assessment**: Intelligently categorizes questions by difficulty level (Easy, Medium, Hard) based on content complexity
4. **Context Preservation**: Ensures generated questions accurately reflect the source material without hallucination
5. **Answer Validation**: Generates correct answers along with plausible distractors for multiple-choice questions
6. **Mathematical Recognition**: Special handling for mathematical content, formulas, and scientific notation

The AI supports multiple content formats including PDFs (both text-based and scanned), images with text, plain text input, and YouTube video transcripts. Users can review and edit all AI-generated questions before publishing.

### Is Testoza proctoring secure?

Yes, Testoza implements military-grade security measures to ensure exam integrity:

**Browser-Level Protection:**
- Tab switching detection with automatic warnings and logging
- Copy-paste functionality completely disabled (keyboard shortcuts and right-click menu)
- Full-screen enforcement with exit prevention
- Developer tools blocking (F12, Ctrl+Shift+I, Inspect Element)
- Browser console access prevention
- Back button and navigation disable during active tests

**System-Level Security:**
- Screenshot and print screen prevention
- Print functionality blocking
- Clipboard monitoring and control
- Keyboard shortcut interception
- Right-click context menu disable

**Monitoring Features:**
- Real-time violation detection and logging
- Automatic session termination on repeated violations
- IP-based session validation
- Device fingerprinting for authenticity
- Suspicious activity pattern detection

**Additional Safeguards:**
- Secure HTTPS connection (TLS 1.3)
- Encrypted data transmission and storage
- Anti-tampering measures
- Rate limiting to prevent brute force attempts
- Regular security audits and updates

These measures make Testoza suitable for high-stakes examinations, competitive tests, and professional certifications where cheating prevention is critical.

- Use branded email templates for test invitations and results

**Test Interface Customization:**

**Certificate Generation:**

**Enterprise Features:**

These features allow schools, colleges, coaching institutes, and corporations to maintain complete brand consistency while using Testoza's powerful testing infrastructure.

Testoza supports multiple question formats to suit various assessment needs:

**1. Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ)**
- Single correct answer

- Image support in questions and options
- Mathematical formula rendering (LaTeX support)

**2. Multiple Select Questions**
- Multiple correct answers possible
- Partial scoring options
- "Select all that apply" format
- Clear visual distinction from single-select

**3. Fill in the Blanks**
- Single or multiple blanks per question
- Case-sensitive answer options

**4. True/False Questions**
- Binary choice format
- Quick assessment building
- Ideal for concept verification

- Rich text editor with formatting options

### How does the PDF-to-Test feature work?

Testoza's PDF-to-Test feature uses advanced AI to convert any PDF document into a structured test:

**Upload Process:**
1. Upload PDF file (supports text-based and scanned/image PDFs)
2. Select number of questions desired
3. Choose question types (MCQ, Multiple Select, Fill in Blanks, True/False)
4. Set difficulty distribution (Easy:Medium:Hard ratio)

**AI Processing:**
1. **Text Extraction**: OCR technology extracts text from scanned documents
2. **Content Analysis**: AI identifies key concepts, definitions, facts, and relationships
3. **Question Synthesis**: Generates questions based on important content sections
4. **Answer Generation**: Creates correct answers and plausible distractors
5. **Quality Scoring**: Ranks questions by relevance and clarity

**Review & Edit:**
- View all generated questions in an editable interface
- Modify question text, options, and correct answers
- Add images or media to enhance questions
- Reorder questions via drag-and-drop
- Delete unsuitable questions
- Add new manual questions alongside AI-generated ones

**Output:**
- Ready-to-publish test with full proctoring and branding options
- Editable question bank for future use
- Exportable question sets

This feature works best with educational content, textbooks, notes, articles, and study materials.

**5. Embed on Website**
- Get embed code for your website
- Students can start test from your site
- Maintains your branding

**6. QR Code**
- Generate QR code for test
- Scan to start (mobile-friendly)
- Print on physical materials

**Sharing Controls:**
- Set expiration dates for links
- Limit number of attempts per link
- Password protect tests
- Enable/disable sharing options
- Track link performance and usage
